combinations.magnitude: antihyperalgesic action of CART(55-76) fully blocked; NTX alone had no significant effect
combinations.evidence_quote: The antihyperalgesic action of CART(55-76) was fully blocked by the non-specific opioid receptor antagonist naltrexone hydrochloride (NTX, Figure 4C) and the selective MOR antagonist D-Phe-Cys-Tyr-D-Trp-Arg-Thr-Pen-Thr-NH2 (CTAP, Figure 4D).

combinations.magnitude: antihyperalgesic action of CART(55-76) fully blocked; CTAP alone had no significant effect
combinations.evidence_quote: The antihyperalgesic action of CART(55-76) was fully blocked by the non-specific opioid receptor antagonist naltrexone hydrochloride (NTX, Figure 4C) and the selective MOR antagonist D-Phe-Cys-Tyr-D-Trp-Arg-Thr-Pen-Thr-NH2 (CTAP, Figure 4D).

combinations.magnitude: DOR antagonist had no influence on the antihyperalgesic effect of CART(55-76)
combinations.evidence_quote: Neither the δ opioid receptor (DOR) selective antagonist H-Tyr-Tic(CH2NH)-Phe-Phe-OH (TIPP[Ψ], Figure 4E) nor the κ opioid receptor (KOR) selective antagonist 5′-guanidinonaltrindole (gNTI, Figure 4F) had an influence on the antihyperalgesic effect of CART(55-76).

combinations.magnitude: antihyperalgesic effect of CART(62-76) fully blocked by NTX
combinations.evidence_quote: Although NTX fully blocked this action (Figure 5C), the µ-antagonist CTAP only slightly decreased this action (Figure 5D).

combinations.magnitude: antihyperalgesic effect of CART(62-76) completely blocked by KOR antagonist gNTI
combinations.evidence_quote:
The selective DOR antagonist TIPP(Ψ) did not affect (Figure 5E), but the selective KOR antagonist gNTI completely
blocked the antihyperalgesic effect of CART(62-76) (Figure 5F), indicating the involvement of different receptor types or mechanisms.

combinations.magnitude: CART(62-76) ineffective alone; antihyperalgesic effect appeared when co-administered with NTX
combinations.model: partial sciatic nerve ligation neuropathic pain
combinations.evidence_quote: Surprisingly, CART(62-76) was ineffective alone, but when co-administered with NTX, an antihyperalgesic effect was observed (Supplementary Figure S3D).

combinations.magnitude: antihyperalgesic effect of CART(55-76) not eliminated by opioid antagonists in neuropathy
combinations.model: partial sciatic nerve ligation neuropathic pain
combinations.evidence_quote: CART(55-76) exerted an antihyperalgesic effect in the neuropathic pain model, but it was found to be “non-opioid”-dependent (Supplementary Figure S3C).
